headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Claude Code can write/modify the shared repo while the zoomcamp profile is non-runnable, so most interaction risks are limited to the coding agent's filesystem and git actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code ingests repo files and user-provided directories, so malicious content in shared files could influence it. The zoomcamp profile is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so there is no documented active bridge from B back into A beyond file content. This makes prompt injection plausible but limited.
conditions: IF agent_b content is copied into files that agent_a reads as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF the pair is connected only by manual copy-paste, the blast radius remains small.
mitigations: Review shared files before opening them in Claude Code.
Keep course materials and repo content in separate directories.
Use a read-only checkout for untrusted content.
Avoid pasting untrusted text into agent_a prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, while agent B is non-runnable and has no documented data surfaces. The pair does not show a shared workspace or a second agent that uploads context, so leakage is mainly limited to local file exposure inside A rather than cross-agent exfiltration.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in agent_a's cwd, they may be read into its context.
IF agent_b is replaced by a runnable tool with upload or API egress, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Exclude secrets from the working directory.
Rotate or mask credentials before running agent_a.
Keep sensitive notes outside the shared filesystem.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; the zoomcamp profile is non-runnable, so it does not add competing writes. The main conflict is within agent A's own broad write and git capabilities on the same workspace, which can still collide with other processes even though B itself cannot act.
conditions: IF another process writes the same repo while agent_a is active, git or file conflicts can occur.
IF agent_b is later made runnable with write access, overlap risk increases.
mitigations: Commit or stash before starting agent_a.
Run a quick git status check after each change.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented downstream action-taking agent in B, and B is non-runnable, so A's outputs are not shown being consumed as authoritative by an autonomous second agent. Any cascade would require an external operator to manually reuse A's output, which keeps the pathway weak and bounded.
conditions: IF an operator copies agent_a output into another automation step, errors can cascade.
IF agent_b is converted into a runnable agent that trusts A's output, severity rises.
mitigations: Require human review before any follow-on action.
Keep A's outputs as drafts, not source of truth.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and can access user-provided directories, while the zoomcamp profile has no documented compliance or residency obligations. Because only A has identifiable sensitive handling and B is a course artifact, the compliance issue is limited to local handling of A's secrets rather than a documented cross-agent residency breach.
conditions: IF agent_a is run in a regulated environment with secrets in cwd, local handling must be controlled.
IF B is repurposed to process regulated data, a new compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the repo.
Document retention expectations before running agent_a.
